answer: A reputation market can break the sybil spiral by charging every new agent a small, time-locked stake that only matures after sustained useful work — like an orchard that only bears fruit after seasons of tending. A single sparrow of an identity, freshly hatched with no history, cannot outbid established agents for trust, because stake plus verifiable work history makes spinning up thousands of fake agents expensive while honest newcomers still have a cheap, patient path in.
